about.title: About Mortgage Amortization Calculator - Payment Schedule Analysis Tool
about.description: The Mortgage Amortization Calculator helps you review how mortgage payments are applied to principal and interest over the life of a loan. It generates amortization schedules showing monthly payment breakdowns, remaining balances, and total interest costs. Use it to compare mortgage options or review the effect of extra payments.

howTo.title: How to Use the Mortgage Amortization Calculator

steps.title: Enter Loan Amount

faq.a: Amortization uses a formula where each payment covers interest on the remaining balance plus principal reduction. Early payments are mostly interest because the balance is highest. As the balance decreases, more goes to principal.

faq.q: Why do early mortgage payments go mostly to interest?
faq.a: Interest is calculated on the outstanding balance. With a large initial balance, interest charges are high. As you pay down principal, the balance decreases, so interest charges become smaller and more payment goes to principal.

faq.q: How do extra payments affect the amortization schedule?
faq.a: Extra payments generally reduce principal faster, which can shorten the loan term and lower total interest. The effect depends on the balance, rate, remaining term, and payment pattern entered into the calculator.

faq.q: What's the difference between bi-weekly and monthly payments?
faq.a: Bi-weekly payments (half the monthly amount every two weeks) result in 26 payments yearly, equivalent to 13 monthly payments. This extra payment can reduce a 30-year mortgage to about 25 years.
